html:
The Wali Songo, or nine saints, are the Muslim teachers who, by Javanese tradition, spread Islam across Java in the 15th and 16th centuries. Their tombs on the north coast are among the busiest pilgrimage sites in Indonesia.

They are linked with the port of Demak, whose sultanate (see Demak) overthrew the Hindu court of Majapahit. Tradition says they used local arts, such as wayang puppet plays and gamelan music, to teach the new faith.

Many of the stories are legend, but they explain why Javanese Islam blends easily with older custom and Sufi mysticism. That style survives in the Nahdlatul Ulama, the largest Muslim group in the world.
